newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore oil products steady in quiet market.
newsitem.headline: Singapore oil products steady in quiet market.

text.p: The Singapore oil products were steady on Wednesday in quiet trade in the absence of fresh direction, traders said.
Gas oil was level despite falls overnight in the west after the release of bearish heating oil stock data in the U.S.
The market was supported by prompt buying interest from a local trader, who had already bought two cargoes this week.
The same trader purchased Wednesday 150,000-barrels Jan 23-27 loading gas oil at $32.30 per barrel free-on-board Singapore from a European major, 15 cents more than Tuesday's traded level.
A major offered 150,000-barrels February 2-6 loading gas oil at $31.75 fob Singapore.
Front-month January swaps traded to an intra-day low of $31.60 a barrel before picking up late in the day to $31.95.

Traders said the prompt gas oil market was balanced but there was some downward pressure as China was not expected to buy as much in February as it has done fo December and January due to the Lunar New Year.
The increase in South Korean refining capacity will weigh on the market in later months but Korea's December and January surplus has been easily absorbed by China.

A Dutch trader bid for a 92-octane gasoline cargo lifting late January at $26.30 a barrel fob, up 10 cents from Tuesday bid level. But no fixed price sellers were heard in the market as traders said they preferred to sell on a floating basis, related to the stronger naphtha spot quotes. Some traders assessed 95-octane around $1.50 per barrel over naphtha quotes.

Naphtha prices were also steady but levels were close to early December's peaks of $26.15 per barrel. Sentiment was strong with good demand heard from North Asia. Yukong Ltd said it restarted its 15,000-bpd reformer Jan 6 despite strong naphtha prices as higher BTX prices helped improve margins.
